verdict: AppLovin grew revenue 68% to $1.41B and kept 59 cents of every dollar as profit — net income nearly doubled to $836M as its AXON ad platform kept compounding.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in 2025, so this platform is the whole company.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the AXON ad platform — down 46% YoY after the apps-business sale shrank the company.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to advertisers and app publishers — down 23% YoY.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed hot
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 68% to $1.41B as advertisers kept shifting budgets to AXON, AppLovin's AI ad platform.

takeaways.title: Most of it became profit
takeaways.text: Net income of $836M is 59% of revenue, up 92% in a year — software costs almost nothing extra to deliver, so growth drops nearly straight to the bottom line.

takeaways.title: Cash in, buybacks out
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $1.05B in a single quarter. AppLovin spent $571M buying back its own shares and raised its buyback authorization by another $3.2B.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $51M on AppLovin's debt, plus $7M of other expense, net.
footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. Its former apps business was sold in 2025 and appears as discontinued operations in earlier periods; there were none this quarter.
